But as you can see, it's incoherent for 2 reasons : 

1 : quarkus.datasource.reactive.url=postgresql://localhost:5432/dbuser

=> this line shouldn't be part of the file since the reactive datasource is specialized (.react.)

BUT if i don"t set it, I got this incoherent error : Error obtaining database connection for healthcheck of datasource '<default>': io.vertx.pgclient.PgExc
eption: { "message": "authentification par mot de passe ?chou?e pour l'utilisateur  ....



2 : quarkus.datasource.react.health-exclude=true

=> if I don't set the reactive datasource as exluded I got this error : 

SRHCK01000: Error processing Health Checks: io.quarkus.runtime.configuration.ConfigurationException: quarkus.datasource.react.jdbc.url has not been defined

In the healthcheck json result, nothing has been exclude...

The healthcheck should work without excluding anything, just separate jdbc from reactive.

@geniusit  Can you try adding this to your original config?

```properties
# Disable the default reactive datasource
quarkus.datasource.reactive.enabled=false
# Disable the react JDBC datasource
quarkus.datasource.react.jdbc.enabled=false
```

When you define a datasource, both the JDBC and Reactive parts are prepared unless you explicitly disable them.
That's why, I think, you get a failing `default` reactive datasource and a failing `react` JDBC datasource in your health check.

@jmartisk @cescoffier while looking into this, I noticed that, in #13375, we got a way to exclude a datasource from health-checks. Yet the implementation for reactive datasources is missing. I'll work on it.

@geniusit sorry I made a mistake, actually you need this:

```properties
# Disable the default reactive datasource
quarkus.datasource.reactive=false
# Disable the react JDBC datasource
quarkus.datasource.react.jdbc=false
```
